Group authoritarianism

1 Study and sample

The group authoritarianism score (group_rwa) was measured in waves 4 and 5. Scored N per wave: 500, 500. No respondent is excluded, a provisional rule (decision log D22).

2 Items and coding

Items (guide reference: Stellmacher and Petzel (2005)). Response scale: 1 = strongly disagree, 4 = neither, 7 = strongly agree. Non-answer codes observed: 0.
Item Wording Facet Waves Direction
group_rwa_1 A group member who has violated group rules should be punished severely. 4, 5
group_rwa_2 A group member may act differently from demands of group rules. 4, 5 reverse-keyed; already reversed in the extract, used as stored
group_rwa_3 If a group member does not agree with decisions of a group leader, he or she should not follow his orders. 4, 5 reverse-keyed; already reversed in the extract, used as stored
group_rwa_4 A group member should always obey group rules. 4, 5
group_rwa_5 A group member has not necessarily to be punished very hard if he has offended against group rules once. 4, 5 reverse-keyed; already reversed in the extract, used as stored
group_rwa_6 Instructions of group leaders should be obeyed under all circumstances. 4, 5

Score. group_rwa is the mean of its 6 items in the scored direction (higher = more group authoritarianism), computed when at least 5 are valid. Scoring rules and names are provisional until the lead signs off (decision log D4, D21, D6).

7 Adjusted model

OLS of group authoritarianism on demographics and left-right self-placement, wave 4. Outcome and numeric predictors in SD units, so group terms are differences in outcome SDs. R² = 0.08. N = 457.
Term Beta [95% CI]
Female (vs male) 0.08 [-0.10, 0.25]
Age -0.01 [-0.10, 0.08]
Entrance qualification (vs none) 0.05 [-0.17, 0.27]
University degree (vs no entrance qualification) -0.32 [-0.55, -0.09]
Household income band 0.06 [-0.04, 0.15]
East (vs West) 0.09 [-0.12, 0.30]
Berlin (vs West) -0.30 [-0.68, 0.07]
Left-right self-placement (right = high) 0.20 [0.11, 0.29]

The model describes associations in this sample. Education groups are provisional (decision log D26), and “another gender” is excluded from the model as too small to estimate.

8 Change over time

Wave means. Analytic N = 500. Self-rated attention subset: N = 487/488. The extract has no instructed-response attention flags, so this subset is a provisional robustness check (Q3).

Mean change from wave 4, random-intercept model (lme4). 500 respondents, 1000 observations.
Contrast Change [95% CI]
wave 5 vs wave 4 0.04 [-0.05, 0.12]
Check of the change estimates with a Bayesian random-intercept model (brms, Stan; 4 chains; prior normal(0, 1) on each contrast).
Contrast lme4 [95% CI] brms [95% CrI] R-hat Bulk ESS
wave 5 vs wave 4 0.04 [-0.05, 0.12] 0.04 [-0.05, 0.13] 1.00 5463

The two methods agree: the largest difference between estimates is < 0.001 scale points, and the largest R-hat is 1.001.

Rank-order stability: Pearson correlation of scores between waves, adjacent and longer intervals.

9 Measurement notes

  • The six items were asked only in waves 4 and 5, so change over time rests on one interval and longer-run stability cannot be estimated.
  • Items 2, 3 and 5 are worded against the construct. The guide does not mark them as reversed. Their stored values correlate positively with the other items in both waves, so the extract already holds them reversed (decision log D6). The fielded instrument should confirm this (Q2).

10 Reproducing this report

Rebuild with Rscript run.R. Package versions are pinned in renv.lock, and every coding decision is in the decision log.

 

Aggregate results only. Study E is a pseudonymous, embargoed extract; no respondent records are published.
